home-start.heading: What brings you and your door in today?

content.title: Choose your starting point.
content.intro: Describe what is happening. Jeff will supply the vocabulary, including several words for oak.

options.label: A new door
options.title: Start with the room and the opening.
options.body: Think about room use, privacy, and where the open door could sit. Keep a photo of the whole wall ready.

options.label: Replace a door
options.summary: A new chapter for this opening.
options.title: Show us what is there now.
options.body: Note what you want to change and what should stay. Photos of the current door and hardware help explain both.

options.label: Fix the movement
options.summary: A scrape, a wobble, or a new opinion.
options.title: Describe what changed.
options.body: Note where it catches and what has changed. Do not force a sticking door or adjust hardware for a better video.

content.note: This choice changes the guidance below. It sends nothing and does not book a visit.

installation-scope.heading: Give the door a plan. Give Doreen a copy.

content.title: What goes in the proposal?
content.intro: Record the work, responsibilities, and open decisions. Doreen can file that. Jeff’s encouraging nod is harder to retrieve.

The finish condition expected at handover

content.title: From first notes to final checks.
content.intro: A planning outline; no project or visit is scheduled here.

steps.title: Describe the opening
steps.body: Gather the room’s purpose, photos, and the change you want.

steps.title: Review the site and materials
steps.body: Check site conditions and compatible products before ordering.

steps.title: Agree on the work and timing
steps.body: Settle scope, supply, price, and the schedule. Doreen then releases the pencil.

steps.title: Walk through the result
steps.body: Review operation, finish, care, and anything left to resolve.

content.note: Sequence and timing depend on the agreed project. This is not a live tracker or completion record.

replacement-materials.heading: Keep what works. Discuss what does not.

content.title: Compare materials before products.
content.intro: Decide what the new door should bring to the room. Jeff votes grain; you still get the casting vote.

rows.name: Visible wood grain
rows.character: Warmth and variation; every board will have its own appearance.
rows.care: Ask for the actual finish manufacturer’s care guidance.
rows.confirm: Species, finish sample, weight, and compatibility with the proposed hardware.

rows.name: Painted finish
rows.character: A color decision that can join the room or deliberately interrupt it.
rows.care: Confirm the coating and the touch-up approach before ordering.
rows.confirm: Construction, color sample, edge details, and responsibility for painting.

rows.name: Glass or glazed design
rows.character: A different conversation about light and privacy.
rows.care: Use guidance for the selected glass, frame, and hardware.
rows.confirm: The product’s intended use, privacy level, safety requirements, and installation instructions.

content.note: Design directions only. Verify the actual product and any retained hardware; affection does not make the holes line up.

hardware-next-step.heading: The track is part of the door conversation.

content.title: The model number matters.
content.body: A photograph shows the part. A model number gets you to its instructions.
points: Keep the product link or model number if you have it.
Photograph the whole installation and any visible labels without dismantling it.
Describe the problem and which parts you hope to retain.
content.action: If the problem is how it moves

content.title: Agree on what happens next.
content.intro: Record the work and agree how to get help afterward. Missing the door is not a service interval.

items.title: Record what was addressed
items.body: Review the agreed work and note any issue that remains unresolved.

items.title: Keep the care and contact details
items.body: Confirm product guidance, the appropriate contact, and any written terms that apply.

items.title: Describe the new behavior
items.body: Note when the issue started and what you can observe safely. Confirm any further visit directly.

content.boundary: If the door appears loose or unsafe, stop using it and arrange appropriate help. Do not dismantle or force it for a photo.
content.note: No warranty, return visit, response time, or check-in is promised here. Agree any follow-up directly. Doreen books appointments; Jeff’s wave from the driveway does not count.

gallery-finishes.heading: Three finishes. Jeff needs a minute.

content.title: Which direction feels right?
content.intro: Compare illustrative designs. These are different doors, not recolors of one product.

options.label: Warm walnut
options.description: Rich grain, strong presence. Jeff has pulled up a chair.
options.alt: Illustrative dark walnut sliding barn door in an interior
options.caption: AI-generated design illustration; not a completed Jeff project or an exact finish sample.

options.label: Quiet oak
options.description: Lighter wood, plenty of grain. “Quiet” describes the door, not the meeting.
options.alt: Illustrative flush oak sliding door showing its natural grain
options.caption: AI-generated design illustration; confirm the actual wood and finish with a physical sample.

options.label: Painted pantry
options.description: Let the room lead. Jeff is learning to share the attention.
options.alt: Illustrative white painted sliding door at a pantry opening
options.caption: AI-generated design illustration; not a product color reference or completed installation.

content.note: The choice is not saved and places no order. Confirm a physical sample and compatible products for actual work.

gallery-story.heading: The pantry that wanted a little dignity.

content.title: A quieter front for a very busy cupboard.
content.alt: Illustrative painted sliding door in front of a pantry
content.caption: AI-generated illustration. This fictional design study does not document a customer project.
content.label: Fictional design study
content.challenge: The imagined brief: make the pantry feel part of the kitchen while keeping everyday access in the conversation. Jeff initially proposed a formal introduction to the cereal.
content.approach: Discuss sightlines, available wall space, handle position, and a real finish sample before choosing a door. Doreen has removed the cereal introduction from the scope.

content.title: Two people. One level.
content.intro: Jeff wants a good door. Doreen wants a finished day. Lenny has one question about the horizontal.

people.name: Jeff
people.role: Doors, and matters arising from doors
people.bio: Remembers a door by its grain and a house by its door. His directions are difficult to follow.
people.aside: Originally from Dallas. You will not have to ask.

people.name: Doreen
people.role: Scope, scheduling, and getting home on time
people.bio: Keeps one calendar, a numbered proposal, and a pen Jeff cannot borrow. Makes room for his ideas when they fit the job.
people.aside: Has never written “whenever the door is ready.”

people.name: Lenny
people.bio: Quiet, consistent, and immune to persuasion. Jeff has tried turning him around. Same answer.

content.note: Parody cast: these biographies are fictional. Lenny is a level. Staffing and responsibilities for actual work must be confirmed directly.

about-notes.heading: Doreen would like this on the record.

content.title: A brief account of a long door conversation.
content.intro: A fictional Tuesday in the field office.

entries.label: 08:10 · Preparation
entries.title: Jeff has brought a second tape measure.
entries.body: The first tape measure has done nothing wrong. Jeff says it is helpful for the numbers to have a witness.
entries.author: Doreen

entries.label: 10:35 · Materials
entries.title: The sample board is now in the passenger seat.
entries.body: It was catching the light better there. The seat belt was my idea. The name was Jeff’s.
entries.author: Doreen

entries.label: 15:20 · Close of business
entries.title: No further comment.
entries.body: The bubble is between the lines. The rest is a management decision.
entries.author: Lenny, as interpreted by Doreen

about-credentials.heading: A fondness for doors is not a credential.

content.title: The paperwork has to stand on its own.
content.intro: Qualifications need current evidence. Enthusiasm has its own section.

items.title: Licensing and registration
items.detail: Confirm the identity, applicable requirements, and current records for the actual contractor and work.

items.title: Insurance
items.detail: Request current evidence and confirm what it covers. This page makes no insurance claim.

items.title: Product or trade credentials
items.detail: Verify any claimed training or authorization with its issuer. Lenny’s attendance does not constitute certification.

pricing-drivers.heading: Four places an estimate can grow.

content.title: Ask what is included.
content.intro: For each line item, agree who supplies it, who does it, and where the work ends.

items.title: The door and its hardware
items.body: The selected products, delivery, and who is ordering them.

items.title: The existing opening
items.body: Access, obstructions, and preparation before fitting can begin.

items.title: The finish line
items.body: Painting, trim, repairs, cleanup, and disposal. “Finished” needs a shared meaning.

items.title: Changes after agreement
items.body: Agree on added work, cost, and timing first. “Jeff had a thought” is not a change order.

contact-prep.heading: A little prep. A manageable amount of Jeff.

content.title: A short list for the conversation.
content.intro: Tick off what you have. Leave unknowns as unknowns.
items: The general location and which opening needs attention
A description of the goal or problem, in your own words
Photos you already have of the wall, door, and visible hardware
Product names or instructions, if available
Questions about access, timing, supplies, and what the scope includes
content.note: These ticks are not sent or saved by the site and do not book a visit. Photos stay with you. Doreen accepts “I don’t know yet” as a complete sentence.

service-area-availability.heading: A town. A date. Doreen has a pencil.

content.title: Let Doreen check the route.
content.body: Include your town and any timing constraints. Jeff finding his keys is not confirmation.
content.note: No live coverage check or appointment booking is available. Confirm the location, visit, and timing directly.

faq-handover.heading: The questions to keep after the door is in.

content.title: Leave with answers.
content.intro: Use these questions at the walkthrough. Jeff can work on his farewell while you check the paperwork.

groups.title: Operation and the agreed finish
items: How should the selected door and hardware be used?
Does the result match the written scope?
What remains open, and who is handling it?

groups.title: Product and care information
groups.body: Keep guidance for the products actually installed.
items: Where are the product names and manufacturer instructions?
Which care instructions apply to this finish?
What should prompt you to stop using the door and ask for help?

groups.title: Contact and any written terms
groups.body: Agree on the practical next step if a question comes up.
items: Who is the right contact?
What warranty or service terms, if any, were agreed?
How will unresolved items be recorded and followed up?

content.note: A question list is not a completion record, acceptance, or warranty. Neither is Jeff’s farewell.

reviews-featured.heading: The door has declined to comment.

content.eyebrow: A note from the Jeff universe
content.title: ‘He remembered the door’s birthday.’
content.quote: I mentioned it had been a year. Jeff brought a card. The envelope was addressed to the pantry. I opened it anyway, and now he’s being a little formal with me.
content.name: An entirely fictional pantry owner
content.reply: The calendar entry has been removed. Jeff has asked whether the door at least saw the card.
